messages:
Sam W: Quick sync — prospect Aurelia Health wants to run a week-long POC. Must-haves: IdP-initiated SAML SSO, SCIM user provisioning with delta syncs, and RBAC mapped to AD group membership. They also want domain-level controls (multiple domains). Can we confirm supported flows and any ops blockers? cc @Maya P @Lucas G

Maya P: We support SP- and IdP-initiated SAML out of the box. For SCIM we have a SCIM 2.0 endpoint that supports /Users bulk and patch. AD group -> role mapping is supported but needs role mapping config on onboarding. Domain verification can be multi-domain but requires DNS TXT ownership for each root domain.

Lucas G: Adding infra notes: Dedicated customers can run SCIM sync from our private endpoint inside their VPC (no public egress). For hosted customers we provide a long-lived SCIM token that rotates on request. If they want SCIM over mutual TLS that's currently custom work.

Sam W: Pricing Q — they asked if SCIM sync volume affects hosted pricing (token/requests) or if it's part of Dedicated reserved capacity. What's the right message to give?

Alisha R: For hosted: SCIM requests are metered under 'admin API' category — small per-request cost; not token-based. For Dedicated: SCIM is included in the reservation for normal control-plane calls, but extremely high delta rates (>>100k users/day) should be scoped as an add-on. We should ask expected users and daily delta rate.

Sam W: Got it. They also flagged security questionnaire item: "Do you support signed SAML assertions and enforce audience restriction?" and "How do you handle SCIM service account key rotation?"

Maya P: Yes, we validate signed assertions and enforce audience+recipient checks. We also publish our SAML metadata endpoint: https://meta.redwood.ai/saml/metadata (include in SSO config). For SCIM keys: we support manual rotation via console + API and can set an automated rotation policy via a Managed Services runbook for Private deployments.

Lucas G: FYI — there is a known edge-case where AD group IDs change on sync, which can cause transient role mismatches. We mitigate with a 5-min reconciliation job and idempotent role bindings. We should tell them about reconciliation window.

Sam W: They require domain proofing per subdomain (aurelia-prod.example, aurelia-staging.example). Is DNS TXT per subdomain acceptable?

Alisha R: For security we require proof of control at the domain root. For subdomain-only claims we can accept either TXT at subdomain or CNAME delegation depending on their DNS model. We'll surface that in the onboarding checklist.

Sam W: Ops blockers: they want IP allowlist of our SCIM callbacks, and an SLA >99.9 for SSO. Can we commit?

Lucas G: SLA: for Dedicated we can offer SLA >99.9 with an uptime bundle. Hosted SLA for production tier is 99.9 as well but requires enterprise contract. IP allowlist — yes, we can support static egress ranges for Dedicated; for hosted we provide a set of outbound CIDRs but low-latency customers sometimes prefer VPC peering.

DeployBot: Reminder: created onboarding ticket #ONB-4821 for Aurelia Health (owner: Maya P).

Maya P: Action items: 1) Sam — ask Aurelia for expected user count and delta sync rate. 2) Lucas — prepare short note on reconciliation window and any custom work (mTLS for SCIM). 3) Alisha — draft pricing note for SCIM delta add-on thresholds and Dedicated SLA language. 4) I'll attach SAML metadata and SCIM base URL examples to the ticket.

Sam W: Will do. One more ask from legal: they want KMS/HSM details for service account keys and audit logs retention. Who owns that answer?

Alisha R: Security owns KMS integration details. For Hosted we use customer-managed keys (CMK) via partner KMS integrations for Private; for Dedicated we can support Bring-Your-Own-KMS (BYOK). Audit logs retention is configurable; default 90 days, enterprise plan can get 1 year or custom on request.

Sam W: Perfect — I'll collect numbers from them and update #ONB-4821. Thanks all :thumbsup:
